We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:
  • Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge
  • Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill
  • Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
  • Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
  • Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create
  • Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
  • Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth
A detailed overview of our benefits is here.

What you're wondering

  • What tools will I use? Figma, Thumbtack (our design system in Figma and Storybook), Claude and Claude Code, Linear, Fibery, PostHog, Notion and Slack. The product is Rails and React with TypeScript
  • What does success look like? By 30 days you can answer a Support question about a stuck check without me. By 60 you own one of the Q4 items end to end with the plan written into Linear. By 90 I'm out of Marketplace standups and you're the named design owner on the Marketplace roadmap
  • How does the design team actually use AI? Designers here ship real PRs, written with Claude against our product and design system repos and reviewed by an engineer like anyone else's. We prototype in code rather than Figma for anything complex, and we've built AI that checks AI: a design code review skill that runs before a PR, plus design system and token compliance checks. Claude still misses the last mile on padding, states and tokens, so human review is mandatory and nothing ships without it
  • Is there really no research function? No dedicated researcher, and there won't be one. There is a documented method set, discussion guide templates, and a live list of customers who have agreed to talk to us, with the intro coming warm from their CSM. What's been missing on Marketplace is the time to use it: for two quarters I've been the designer, the PM and the Head of Design at once. You'd have the access. We want someone who can make a good call fast, then pull the squad back toward research backed judgement as the default
data.description:
Hi 👋 I'm Elvin, Head of Design at Pinpoint.

We build and sell software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire and onboard the right people. We're a team of about 100 across the UK, EU and US, with a mature product, strong product market fit and happy customers.

Inside Pinpoint sits a part of the product most ATSs don't have: background checks, right to work, reference checks, one way video interviews and the credits and billing that power them. We call it Marketplace. It's the squad behind the revenue that scales with how much customers use us, and an important strategic bet towards continued growth.

For the past two quarters I've been its designer, its PM and the Head of Design at the same time. The next phase is harder than what we've already shipped, and it needs someone whose whole job it is, which is why we're hiring a Staff Product Designer.

That's where you come in. You'll be the only designer on the Marketplace squad, working alongside our Head of Commercial Product (the squad's PM), our Tech Lead, a Senior Product Engineer, and our Head of Roadmap Engineering.

What you should know up front
  • This is a remote role based in the UK, Portugal, Spain or Poland, working UK hours, with a few in person team meetups a year. We're headquartered in Jersey
  • The product is a set of status driven workflows: a check gets ordered, a vendor or a regulator decides what happens next, and the design has to handle every outcome, including the ones that fail. Our third party vendors set what's possible and the compliance rules are fixed, so you'll spend as much time understanding how a vendor actually behaves as you do in Figma
  • AI is how we work, not a tool we're trialling. I ship my own PRs through Claude Code now, and I hadn't shipped one 3 months ago. You don't need to have done that yet, but you do need to be using AI across your work today and to want to learn
  • There's no dedicated researcher. Decisions have been quick and under pressure for a while. We want someone who can make a good call fast and who also pulls the squad toward research backed judgement as the norm
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions
data.key_responsibilities:
• Own design for every usage based feature in Pinpoint end to end, from the first conversation with a vendor or customer through the spec and the design to shipped and measured
  • Ship the next phase of Pinpoint Checks, including the DBS update service with automated routing, rechecks, sending check data to downstream systems, decision and audit flows, and the UK high compliance checks that follow
  • Turn credits from something customers are given into something they understand and use. Credit visibility, self serve costing and in platform credit management are being scoped now and they are yours to design
  • Shape Marketplace product strategy with the PM going into 2027, then execute on it. Discovery here is shared between you and the PM, not handed to you
  • Write the plan into the ticket before anything is built, with the decisions made, the edge cases covered and the questions closed, so an engineer (or you) can build it with Claude without a second round of questions
  • Prototype in code where it beats Figma, submit your own PRs for small front end fixes, and QA what ships
  • Be the person Support, Sales and Legal come to when a check is stuck or a customer asks what a vendor does with their data. You'll know the domain better than almost anyone in the company within 90 days
  • Bring Marketplace work to weekly design crit and feed new patterns (status cards, order flows, decision recording) back into Thumbtack, our design system
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Design of complex B2B software products alongside a PM and engineers, with shipped work to show for it, ideally as the sole or lead designer
  • A startup or scale up background, with small teams, few handoffs and a willingness to do whatever the product needs that week
  • Hands on work designing around constraints set by someone else, such as a regulator, a compliance rule or a third party vendor's API. Background screening, identity, fintech, payments, insurance and legal are the obvious homes for it, and comparable complexity elsewhere counts
  • Multi state workflows in the portfolio, such as orders, cases, applications and checks, where the system decides the next step and the design has to handle the moments when it can't
  • Familiarity with what changes at enterprise scale, including permissions, configuration, multiple personas, and flows that hold up at 10 users and at 10,000
  • Daily use of AI across the whole job rather than only to produce screens faster, covering research, testing, investigating bugs, prototyping and documenting, plus the technical depth and appetite to learn to ship small PRs with Claude Code
  • Production ready UI craft that clears a high bar, shown in the portfolio
  • Ownership of the call when the data isn't there, from deciding and explaining the reasoning to owning the outcome and solving the problem in front of you whether or not it is strictly a design problem. Over time, pulling the squad towards research backed judgement as the norm
  • Fluency in commercial outcomes, so margin, adoption and conversion get discussed as naturally as flows and components
  • Bonus: HR tech or ATS experience, or credits, billing and usage based pricing
You may not enjoy this role if
  • You want a research team, a brief and a backlog handed to you. Here you write the brief
  • You're waiting to see how the AI thing plays out before changing how you work
  • You'd rather own the design system or lead a team. This is an IC role on one squad, and Thumbtack governance stays with me
  • Your portfolio is agency work or consumer apps only. Marketplace serves enterprise customers ordering checks at volume, and the panel will test for it
data.title: Staff Product Designer

Hi 👋 I'm Emily, Director of Growth Marketing at Pinpoint.

We build and sell software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire and onboard the right people. We're a team of about 100 across the UK, EU and US, with a mature product, strong product market fit and happy customers.

Pinpoint ships fast. Our product team releases new features every few weeks, and some of them change how we talk about the whole product. That pace is one of our biggest advantages, but only if customers, prospects, and our own team actually hear about it. Today most launches get positioned after they've gone live, so good work lands late and quietly.

We need one person to close that gap and be the connection between Product and the rest of the company, which is why we're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager.

That's where you come in. You'll know what's coming before it ships, decide how each feature is positioned, and make sure every launch is ready on day one. That way Sales can sell it and customers adopt it.

What you should know up front
  • This is a remote role based in the UK, with London coworking sessions, quarterly strategy days and the occasional industry event
  • You'll join a marketing team of 6, including you, covering growth, content, customer marketing, events, and marketing ops. You report to me, and as our sole dedicated product marketer, you'll set how product marketing works here
  • The pace is the hard part. Something meaningful ships most weeks, so you'll be working ahead of the roadmap, chasing dates and detail with product managers, and deciding which launches get a big push and which get a light touch
  • The team runs the website, customer campaigns, and events, and Sales owns the deck. You set the positioning and the plan (what's launching, what we call it, why it matters, and who does what), and make the core launch pieces yourself, from the launch copy and one pager to the enablement pack and whatever else the campaign needs
  • We're AI forward. Everyone here uses AI every day to research, write, and build faster, and we'd expect you to bring that into how you plan and make launches
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions
data.key_responsibilities:
• Own how we position every significant feature, from what it's called and who it's for to how it compares, then bring a clear recommendation to Product and leadership, make the call, and keep it consistent everywhere it shows up
  • Translate what we ship into the results customers get, tying features together to show what's possible, backed by proof points and customer stories
  • Sit close enough to Product that nothing is ever released as a surprise. Live in the roadmap in Fibery, read the specs and early designs, keep dates honest with product managers, and decide which launches get a big push and which get a light touch
  • Plan and run each launch with the rest of marketing, from agreeing the customer adoption plan with our customer marketer and briefing content on feature and integrations pages to lining up events, podcasts and social. Then keep good features in market so they don't fade after a week
  • Give Sales the messaging, talk tracks and enablement packs they need to sell what's new, and brief updates to the sales deck
  • Make sure everyone who talks to customers (Sales, CS, Implementation, Support) knows what's shipped, why it matters and how to talk about it, and be the source of truth for product messaging, flagging what's out of date after every priority release and getting it fixed
  • Make what plays to your strengths yourself (product video, social, ad creative, simple designs, launch copy) and brief the rest. If you're great at one of them, it's yours
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Product marketing in B2B SaaS, with features positioned and launched end to end and the work to show for it
  • A track record of running launches across product, content, sales and customer marketing, with briefs that come back right first time
  • Technical depth to get into how the product works and explain it simply to any audience
  • Time in a startup or scale up, with small teams, few handoffs and the drive to deliver without hand holding
  • Strategy and making in the same day, from positioning in the morning to a launch banner in the afternoon. No need to be a designer, but good taste and the skills to make a banner, slide, page or short video that looks right
  • Early involvement with product teams, in the roadmap and the specs before anything ships, and the ability to turn a spec, a roadmap entry or a rough demo into positioning people actually use
  • The judgement to stop and ask what a launch is meant to achieve, whether it's working and when to change course
  • Strong writing that's clear, simple and straight to the point, with plain copy over clever copy, fewer words over more, and a high bar for quality in everything that goes out
  • An AI forward way of working, using AI every day to research, write and make things faster, even building simple tools to make launch assets
You may not enjoy this role if
  • You'd rather write the strategy than ship the launch
  • You need a big team, a designer or an agency to get things out the door
  • You can't get to London for quarterly strategy days and in person meetings
data.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager

Hi 👋 I'm Mountain, Head of Technical Success at Pinpoint.

We build and sell software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire and onboard the right people. We're a team of about 100 across the UK, EU and US, with a mature product, strong product market fit and happy customers.

Technical Success clears the technical path for everyone who touches a customer. When Sales, Customer Success or Implementation hits something complex inside the platform (a careers site change, a bulk data job through our API, an integration, a migration, an escalation nobody else can crack), it lands with us. We've just welcomed our first Senior Technical Success Engineer, and we're expanding how the team works around automation and AI rather than more hands on the queue. We want the next person to help build that, which is why we're hiring a second Senior Technical Success Engineer.

That's where you come in. You look at a queue of tickets and see the workflow behind them. You'd rather fix the pattern than close the ticket, you reach for AI to do it, and you check what it gives you before a customer ever sees it. You won't know every technology on day one, but you're the kind of person who figures it out.

What you should know up front
  • This is a remote role based in the UK, Spain, Portugal or Poland, with occasional in person team meetups
  • You'd report to me, inside R&D, working alongside a small team and partnering every day with Customer Success, Implementation, Sales and our engineers
  • This is not a support role. Support is reactive; this role exists to remove the reasons support gets called
  • We're an AI first team. AI writes our scripts, builds our tooling and does real work in our workflows, and we expect you to raise that bar, not just meet it
  • Pinpoint is still very much a startup. Priorities shift and not everything is defined, and we want people who do well in that
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions
data.key_responsibilities:
• Build AI workflows, scripts and automations that take apart the repetitive work in careers site changes, bulk data jobs and onboarding, so the queue shrinks instead of grows
  • Solve the technical problems that block customer facing teams, from API and integration work to data migrations and platform configuration
  • Get under the hood of the platform to understand not just what a customer sees, but why it behaves that way and where the real fix lives
  • Turn recurring customer friction into clear signal for the product squads, not just a closed ticket
  • Be the technical partner in the room with customers, able to talk to their IT team and their talent team in the same conversation
  • Build alongside our first Senior Technical Success Engineer to set the standard for how the growing team works
In practice, that means work like:
  • Make careers site changes and fix them when they break, from custom application forms, tracking pixels and HTML and CSS tweaks to embeds that stop working after a customer changes their own site
  • Run bulk data jobs through our API, from mass updates and retagging thousands of records to cleanups and exports
  • Set up and debug integrations, including SSO, job board feeds, HRIS and onboarding handoffs, calendars, and customers' own API and webhook builds
  • Migrate data for customers moving off another ATS, mapping fields, cleaning messy exports and getting it all in clean
  • Crack the escalations no one else can, like the email that didn't send, the sync that failed silently or the config doing something nobody expected
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Hands on technical work for customers across integrations, data, configuration and debugging, ideally at a B2B SaaS company
  • Something you've built with AI and still rely on, such as a workflow, agent or automation that took real work off your plate, not a certificate or a tool you tried once
  • Working code in Python, JavaScript or similar, enough to write and debug your own scripts that call an API, move or clean data, or automate a task, plus an understanding of what's going on underneath any no code tool you use
  • An instinct to fix the system behind a problem, not just the problem in front of you
  • Sound judgment about AI, including knowing when it's confidently wrong and when not to use it at all
  • Comfort with ambiguity, and a habit of figuring things out rather than waiting for a spec
  • Ease in front of a customer as well as under the hood. Most people are one or the other; we need both
  • Motivation to solve customers' technical problems after the sale, rather than to carry a number
  • Bonus: a background in technical support or support engineering where you outgrew the ticket queue and started building your way out of it
You may not enjoy this role if
  • Your AI experience is a course and a forked repo rather than something you built and use
  • You want to stay heads down and never speak to a customer
  • You need every problem to come with a documented answer before you'll touch it
  • You want to architect deep software systems all day. This role is broader and lighter touch than that by design
data.title: Senior Technical Success Engineer
